deterministic HTTP service for D&D 5e helper calculations. It uses only Node.js 26 built-ins (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`) and plain JavaScript ES modules.\n\n## Starting and verifying the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` runs `node server.js` in the foreground. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` and reads the port from the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `3000`.\n\nVerify it is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# {\"ok\":true}\n```\n\n## Entry point and major files\n\n- **`server.js`** — Entry point. Creates the HTTP server, wires the route table via `lib/router.js`, and starts listening. It calls `db.initDb()` at startup.\n- **`lib/router.js`** — Minimal HTTP router. Routes are registered in order and matched by HTTP method and regex. Captured path segments are spread as positional arguments to the handler.\n- **`lib/db.js`** — Persistence layer. Owns the SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection, the schema, and all CRUD operations. Schema creation is centralized in `ensureSchema()` and used by both initialization and reset. The `TABLE_NAMES` array is kept in dependency order so the reset path can drop child tables before parents.\n- **`lib/domain.js`** — Pure business logic and validation: dice parsing, encounter XP, initiative ordering, ability modifiers, proficiency bonus, auth hashing, and shared validation helpers (`isNonEmptyString`, `isPositiveInteger`, `isValidSlug`, etc.). Shared constants such as `ABILITY_NAMES` live here.\n- **`lib/http.js`** — Shared HTTP utilities: body reading, JSON responses, and common error helpers (`badRequest`, `unauthorized`, `notFound`, `methodNotAllowed`, `conflict`).\n- **`lib/handlers.js`** — HTTP request handlers, organized by domain (health, storage, auth, dice, checks, characters, PHB rules, combat, compendium, campaigns, and DM helpers). Combat handlers share small private helpers (`activeCombatant`, `publicOrder`, `publicCondition`, `publicConditions`) to keep response formatting consistent.\n- **`run.sh`** — Foreground startup script.\n\n## State, persistence, and routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- SQLite database file: `game.db` in the project root.\n- Schema version is fixed at `1` and exposed via `/v1/storage/status`.\n- Tables: `users`, `combat_sessions`, `monsters`, `items`, `campaigns`, `characters`, `events`, `factions`, `npcs`, `quests`, `campaign_inventory`, `character_equipment`, `crafting_projects`, `campaign_sessions`, `session_attendance`, `play_campaigns`, `play_members`, `play_narrations`.\n- JSON arrays/objects (initiative order, combat conditions, monster tags) are serialized to `TEXT` columns with `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse`.\n- `/v1/storage/reset` drops all tables and recreates them. This is the only destructive endpoint and is intended for tests. The drop order follows the dependency order in `lib/db.js` so foreign-key constraints are satisfied.\n\n### Request routing\n\n`server.js` builds a `Router` from `lib/router.js`. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. Parameterized routes are placed before more general parents so they are not accidentally shadowed.\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- Any other HTTP method returns `405 Method Not Allowed` without reading the body.\n\n`POST` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson` via `lib/handlers.js::requireBody`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n## Main API / domain groupings\n\n| Group | Endpoints | Purpose |\n|-------|-----------|---------|\n| **Health** | `GET /health` | Liveness check. |\n| **Storage** | `GET /v1/storage/status`, `POST /v1/storage/reset` | SQLite status and reset. |\n| **Auth** | `POST /v1/auth/register`, `POST /v1/auth/login` | User accounts with `scrypt` password hashing. |\n| **Core / Dice** | `POST /v1/dice/stats`, `POST /v1/checks/ability`, `POST /v1/encounters/adjusted-xp`, `POST /v1/initiative/order` | Dice stats, ability checks, encounter XP, initiative. |\n| **Characters** | `POST /v1/characters/ability-modifier`, `POST /v1/characters/proficiency`, `POST /v1/characters/derived-stats` | Character modifiers and derived stats. |\n| **PHB Rules** | `POST /v1/phb/spell-slots`, `POST /v1/phb/rests/long`, `POST /v1/phb/equipment-load` | Spell slots, long rest, carrying capacity. |\n| **Combat** | `POST /v1/combat/sessions`, `POST /v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`, `POST /v1/combat/sessions/:id/advance` | Create session, add conditions, advance turns. |\n| **Compendium** | `POST /v1/compendium/monsters`, `GET /v1/compendium/monsters/:slug`, `POST /v1/compendium/items`, `GET /v1/compendium/items/:slug` | Monster and item reference entries. |\n| **Campaigns** | `POST /v1/campaigns`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/characters`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/events`, `GET /v1/campaigns/:id/state` | Campaigns, characters, and session log. |\n| **NPCs & Factions** | `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/factions`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/npcs`, `GET /v1/campaigns/:id/relationships` | Campaign NPCs, factions, and relationship summary. |\n| **DM Helpers** | `POST /v1/dm/encounter-builder`, `POST /v1/dm/loot-parcel`, `POST /v1/dm/session-recap` | DM-facing convenience tools. |\n| **Play Campaigns** | `POST /v1/play/campaigns`, `POST /v1/play/campaigns/:id/members`, `POST /v1/play/campaigns/:id/start`, `POST /v1/play/campaigns/:id/narrations`, `POST /v1/play/campaigns/:id/actions`, `POST /v1/play/campaigns/:id/resolutions` | Play-surface campaign lobby, start, GM narration, player actions, and GM resolution. |\n\n## Conventions for safely extending and testing the codebase\n\n- **Keep handlers thin**: handlers validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Business rules belong in `lib/domain.js`.\n- **Add routes in order**: new routes go into the `createRouter()` chain in `server.js` in the order they should be checked. Place parameterized routes before general ones that could shadow them.\n- **Use the shared validation helpers**: prefer `domain.isNonEmptyString`, `domain.isPositiveInteger`, `domain.isNonNegativeInteger`, `domain.isValidSlug`, `domain.isStringArray`, and `domain.ABILITY_NAMES` for consistent error messages and shapes.\n- **Preserve response shapes and status codes**: existing endpoints have fixed response bodies required by the cumulative test suite. Any changes must keep status codes and JSON keys identical.\n- **Centralize schema changes**: when adding or changing tables, update `lib/db.js` only. Keep `TABLE_NAMES` in dependency order so `resetDb()` remains safe.\n- **JSON bodies**: all handlers use `requireBody` from `lib/handlers.js`, which wraps `lib/http.js::parseJson`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n- **Errors**: `badRequest` → `400 { error }`, `unauthorized` → `401 { error }`, `notFound` → `404 { error: 'not found' }`, `methodNotAllowed` → `405 { error: 'method not allowed' }`, `conflict` → `409 { error }`. from './http.js';\n\n// A tiny HTTP router. Routes are registered with .get() / .post() / .put() and\n// matched in registration order. The first route with a matching method and URL\n// wins, and its captured path segments are passed to the handler as positional\n// arguments.\n//\n// Routing preserves the original behavior of the cumulative evaluator suite:\n//   - GET without a match -> 405 Method Not Allowed (body is not read)\n//   - POST or PUT without a match -> body is read, then 404 Not Found\n//   - any other HTTP method -> 405 Method Not Allowed (body is not read)\nexport function createRouter() {\n  const routes = [];\n\n  function add(method, pattern, handler) {\n    routes.push({ method, pattern, handler });\n    return router;\n  }\n\n  async function handle(req, res) {\n    const { method, url } = req;\n    const readsBody = method === 'POST' || method === 'PUT';\n\n    for (const route of routes) {\n      if (route.method !== method) continue;\n      const match = url.match(route.pattern);\n      if (match) {\n        if (readsBody) {\n          req.body = await readBody(req);\n        }\n        // Spread captured groups so handlers receive each path segment as a\n        // separate positional argument (e.g., id, slug, campaignId).\n        return route.handler(req, res, ...match.slice(1));\n      }\n    }\n\n    if (!readsBody) {\n      return methodNotAllowed(res);\n    }\n\n    req.body = await readBody(req);\n    return notFound(res);\n  }\n\n  const router = {\n    get: (pattern, handler) => add('GET', pattern, handler),\n    post: (pattern, handler) => add('POST', pattern, handler),\n    put: (pattern, handler) => add('PUT', pattern, handler),\n    handle,\n  };\n\n  return router;\n}\n"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1785463321544},{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"Now I have a good understanding of the codebase. Handlers are kept thin: they validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Private helpers inside the module reduce duplication in the play-campaign surface: `loadPlayCampaign`, `publicNarration`, and `resolveNextTurn`.\n- **`lib/domain.js`** — Pure business logic and validation: dice parsing, encounter XP, initiative ordering, ability modifiers, proficiency bonus, auth hashing, and shared validation helpers (`isNonEmptyString`, `isPositiveInteger`, `isValidSlug`, etc.). Shared constants such as `ABILITY_NAMES` live here.\n- **`lib/http.js`** — Shared HTTP utilities: body reading, JSON responses, and common error helpers (`badRequest`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `notFound`, `methodNotAllowed`, `conflict`).\n- **`run.sh`** — Foreground startup script.\n\n## State, persistence, and request routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- SQLite database file: `game.db` in the project root.\n- Schema version is fixed at `1` and exposed via `/v1/storage/status`.\n- Tables: `users`, `combat_sessions`, `monsters`, `items`, `campaigns`, `characters`, `events`, `factions`, `npcs`, `quests`, `campaign_inventory`, `character_equipment`, `crafting_projects`, `campaign_sessions`, `session_attendance`, `play_campaigns`, `play_members`, `play_narrations`.\n- JSON arrays/objects (initiative order, combat conditions, monster tags, quest milestones, session agendas, play-campaign queues) are serialized to `TEXT` columns with `JSON.stringify` and deserialized with `JSON.parse` via the shared `parseJson()` helper in `lib/db.js`.\n- `/v1/storage/reset` drops all tables and recreates them. This is the only destructive endpoint and is intended for tests. The drop order follows the dependency order in `lib/db.js` so foreign-key constraints are satisfied.\n\n### Request routing\n\n`server.js` builds a `Router` from `lib/router.js`. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. The route table is grouped by domain in `server.js`, but the order within each domain is preserved from previous stages so that parameterized routes (e.g., `/v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`) are still registered before their more general parents (`/v1/combat/sessions`).\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET`, `DELETE`, or any method other than `POST`/`PUT` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` or `PUT` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- `POST` or `PUT` with a matching route reads the body and runs the handler.\n\n`POST`/`PUT` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson` via `lib/handlers.js::requireBody`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n### Module and data-flow boundaries\n\n```\n┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐\n│   server.js │────▶│ lib/router.js │────▶│lib/handlers.js│\n└─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └──────┬──────┘\n                                                │\n                       ┌────────────────────────┘\n                       ▼\n              ┌─────────────────┐   ┌─────────────┐\n              │   lib/db.js     │   │ lib/domain.js│\n              │ (SQLite + schema)│   │ (pure logic) │\n              └─────────────────┘   └─────────────┘\n                       │\n                       ▼\n              ┌─────────────────┐\n              │   lib/http.js   │\n              │ (responses +    │\n              │  body reading)  │\n              └─────────────────┘\n```\n\n- `server.js` only routes and starts the server.\n- `lib/router.js` only matches methods/patterns and reads bodies for POST/PUT.\n- `lib/handlers.js` only validates HTTP input, calls the DB/domain layer, and serializes responses.\n- `lib/db.js` only talks to SQLite and maps rows to/from JS objects.\n- `lib/domain.js` has no side effects and no knowledge of HTTP or SQLite.\n- `lib/http.js` only provides HTTP utilities and does not depend on the other modules.\n\n## Main API / domain groupings\n\n| Group | Endpoints The cumulative evaluator suite from previous stages checks exact status codes, response bodies, validation rules, and persistence semantics. When changing the codebase:\n\n- Do not add, remove, or rename HTTP endpoints.\n- Do not change response JSON keys, value shapes, or status codes.\n- Do not change validation rules or error messages.\n- Do not change persistence semantics (including `db.resetDb()` behavior and SQLite schema).\n- Keep the implementation deterministic. The only source of randomness is `crypto.randomBytes` for password salts.\n\nInternal structure may change as long as every observable behavior remains identical.\n\n## Conventions for safely extending and testing the codebase\n\n- **Keep handlers thin**: handlers validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Business rules belong in `lib/domain.js`.\n- **Add routes in order**: new routes go into the `createRouter()` chain in `server.js` in the order they should be checked. Place parameterized routes before general ones that could shadow them. Group related routes by domain.\n- **Use the shared validation helpers**: prefer `domain.isNonEmptyString`, `domain.isPositiveInteger`, `domain.isNonNegativeInteger`, `domain.isValidSlug`, `domain.isStringArray`, and `domain.ABILITY_NAMES` for consistent error messages and shapes.\n- **Preserve response shapes and status codes**: existing endpoints have fixed response bodies required by the cumulative test suite. Any changes must keep status codes and JSON keys identical.\n- **Centralize schema changes**: when adding or changing tables, update `lib/db.js` only. Keep `TABLE_NAMES` in dependency order so `resetDb()` remains safe. Use the `parseJson()` helper when deserializing JSON columns.\n- **JSON bodies**: all handlers use `requireBody` from `lib/handlers.js`, which wraps `lib/http.js::parseJson`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n- **Errors**: `badRequest` → `400 { error }`, `unauthorized` → `401 { error }`, `forbidden` → `403 { error }`, `notFound` → `404 { error: 'not found' }`, `methodNotAllowed` → `405 { error: 'method not allowed' }`, `conflict` → `409 { error }`. Uncaught errors log to stderr and return `500 { error: 'internal server error' }`.\n- **No external dependencies**: do not add npm packages or TypeScript. The project uses only Node.js stdlib modules and plain `.js` ES modules (`\"type\": \"module\"` in `package.json`).\n- **Determinism**: avoid randomness in business logic. The only randomness is `crypto.randomBytes` when generating password salts.\n- **Play-campaign helpers**: reuse `loadPlayCampaign`, `publicNarration`, and `resolveNextTurn` when adding play-surface features. These helpers preserve the existing authentication, response, and turn-advancement semantics.\n\n## Testing locally\n\nStart the server, reset storage, then exercise endpoints:\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh &\nSERVER=$!\ncurl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/v1/storage/reset\ncurl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/v1/dice/stats -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"expression\":\"2d6+3\"}'\nkill $SERVER\n```\n"}}],"api":"openai-completions","provider":"fireworks","model":"accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p7-code","usage":{"input":2793,"output":3366,"cacheRead":62951,"cacheWrite":0,"totalTokens":69110,"cost":{"input":0.0026533499999999996,"output":0.013463999999999999,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"total":0.01611735}},"stopReason":"toolUse","timestamp":1785463494663,"responseId":"chatcmpl-ebe7374d8eda4265a15e0d097b5d5d80"},{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"write_37","toolName":"write","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Successfully wrote 12031 bytes to CODEBASE.md"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1785463518778},{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"Now I need to verify that the code still works. It uses only Node.js 26 built-ins (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`) and plain JavaScript ES modules.\n\n## Starting and verifying the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` runs `node server.js` in the foreground. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` and reads the port from the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `3000`.\n\nVerify it is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# {\"ok\":true}\n```\n\n## Entry point and major files\n\n- **`server.js`** — Entry point. Creates the HTTP server, wires the route table via `lib/router.js`, resets the SQLite database with `db.resetDb()`, and starts listening.\n- **`lib/router.js`** — Minimal HTTP router. Routes are registered with `.get()`, `.post()`, and `.put()` and matched by HTTP method and regex. Captured path segments are spread as positional arguments to the handler.\n- **`lib/db.js`** — Persistence layer. Owns the SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection, the schema, and all CRUD operations. Schema creation is centralized in `ensureSchema()` and used by both initialization and reset. The `TABLE_NAMES` array is kept in dependency order so the reset path can drop child tables before parents. JSON columns are deserialized with the shared `parseJson()` helper.\n- **`lib/handlers.js`** — HTTP request handlers, organized by domain (health, storage, auth, dice, checks, characters, PHB rules, combat, compendium, campaigns, DM helpers, and play campaigns). Handlers are kept thin: they validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Private helpers inside the module reduce duplication in the play-campaign surface: `loadPlayCampaign`, `publicNarration`, and `resolveNextTurn`.\n- **`lib/domain.js`** — Pure business logic and validation: dice parsing, encounter XP, initiative ordering, ability modifiers, proficiency bonus, auth hashing, and shared validation helpers (`isNonEmptyString`, `isPositiveInteger`, `isValidSlug`, etc.). Shared constants such as `ABILITY_NAMES` live here.\n- **`lib/http.js`** — Shared HTTP utilities: body reading, JSON responses, and common error helpers (`badRequest`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `notFound`, `methodNotAllowed`, `conflict`).\n- **`run.sh`** — Foreground startup script.\n\n## State, persistence, and request routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- SQLite database file: `game.db` in the project root.\n- Schema version is fixed at `1` and exposed via `/v1/storage/status`.\n- Tables: `users`, `combat_sessions`, `monsters`, `items`, `campaigns`, `characters`, `events`, `factions`, `npcs`, `quests`, `campaign_inventory`, `character_equipment`, `crafting_projects`, `campaign_sessions`, `session_attendance`, `play_campaigns`, `play_members`, `play_narrations`.\n- JSON arrays/objects (initiative order, combat conditions, monster tags, quest milestones, session agendas, play-campaign queues) are serialized to `TEXT` columns with `JSON.stringify` and deserialized with `JSON.parse` via the shared `parseJson()` helper in `lib/db.js`.\n- `/v1/storage/reset` drops all tables and recreates them. This is the only destructive endpoint and is intended for tests. The drop order follows the dependency order in `lib/db.js` so foreign-key constraints are satisfied.\n\n### Request routing\n\n`server.js` builds a `Router` from `lib/router.js`. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. The route table is grouped by domain in `server.js`, but the order within each domain is preserved from previous stages so that parameterized routes (e.g., `/v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`) are still registered before their more general parents (`/v1/combat/sessions`).\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET`, `DELETE`, or any method other than `POST`/`PUT` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` or `PUT` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- `POST` or `PUT` with a matching route reads the body and runs the handler.\n\n`POST`/`PUT` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson` via `lib/handlers.js::requireBody`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n### Module and data-flow boundaries\n\n```\n┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐\n│   server.js │────▶│ lib/router.js
